scope_fields.theorem: A positive compatible symplectic surface germ at p has a tangent-line model under the explicit canonical symplectic/statistical Codazzi construction if and only if it admits a local Killing field X with X(p) nonzero.
scope_fields.interpretation: The original item does not define compatible there. The theorem is conditional on the explicit canonical-form/statistical Codazzi interpretation in the proof, with direct calculation and Satoh as support.
scope_clarifications: Real dimension two, one-dimensional Riemannian base, local open tangent-bundle patches.
X must be nonzero at the chosen point; a merely nontrivial local Killing field is insufficient.
The curvature-wedge condition is necessary only, with an explicit insufficiency example.
Levi-Civita-only tangent-line models are precisely locally flat oriented surface germs.
Every constant-curvature surface is locally modeled at every point.
No higher-dimensional characterization, global recognition theorem, or present unrestricted-problem literature status is established.
